Serial restaurant robber gets added time after federal prosecutors push for new indictment

By Lydian Coombs
Published: Aug. 18, 2026 at 6:23 PM EDT|Updated: 11 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:15
Instaread

MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC) - An inmate who is serving a lesser sentence for multiple armed robberies at Memphis fast food restaurants will serve more time after federal prosecutors pushed for a new indictment.

Prosecutors say Clayton Bratcher, 26, robbed two McDonald’s locations and a Taco Bell in July 2023.

Bratcher was identified as the suspect through citizen tips after the Memphis Police Department posted surveillance video from one of the crimes.

Bratcher was initially indicted on all three robbery counts, but the Shelby County District Attorney’s Office dismissed two of them as part of a plea agreement.

Bratcher was sentenced to eight years in prison as a result, but federal prosecutors wanted him to serve time for all three armed robberies.

A federal grand jury issued a new indictment, charging Bratcher with the two charges that the DA’s office dismissed.

Bratcher pleaded guilty to both counts and was subsequently sentenced to 14 years and one day of federal imprisonment, to be followed by five years of supervised release.

The federal sentence will run consecutive to the previously imposed eight-year sentence.
